descs.t: Ethan Klein of H3 has posted an apology and asked the public to respect his family's privacy after Hila Klein revealed he had been having an affair. Posts online name an employee as the other woman, and an old clip of the two women is circulating again. We walk through what has been said, by whom, and what is still only rumor.

Ethan Klein's apology video has drawn far more mockery than sympathy, and his critics, Hasan Piker's audience among them, are treating the affair as proof of everything they said about him. Does a cheating scandal settle the political fights around H3? We separate the affair from the arguments it is being used to win.

Ethan Klein's affair is his own mess, but watch what his enemies are doing with it: a personal betrayal is being turned into a weapon against his support for Israel, often in openly antisemitic language. We look at the scandal, the apology, and the pile on that has nothing to do with his marriage.

intro.plain: Ethan Klein of H3 is in the middle of an affair scandal. Hila Klein revealed it, he has posted an apology and asked for privacy, and the internet has not given him any. I want to go through what is actually known and what is still rumor. Chat, does an apology video ever help in a situation like this?
intro.mid: So Ethan Klein's weird apology is out, and it is not landing. Hila revealed the affair, posts online name an employee, and an old clip of the two women is going around as if it predicted everything. His critics are celebrating. Here is my question for the chat: does his affair change a single argument he made about Hasan?
intro.bold: Ethan Klein cheated on his wife, Hila revealed it, and his enemies could not be happier. But look at what they are doing with it: a broken marriage turned into a license for open hate. You can think he behaved terribly and still see that. Chat, tell me honestly: is this about his marriage, or about his politics?

hook.plain: Hila Klein revealed the affair, and Ethan Klein answered with an apology and a request for privacy. Here is what has actually been said, and what is still rumor.
hook.mid: An old H3 clip is going viral because it seems to show the affair coming. Ethan Klein has apologized. Now his critics want the scandal to settle every old fight.
hook.bold: Ethan Klein's affair is a personal betrayal. What his enemies are doing with it is something else entirely, and it tells you exactly who they are.

descs.t: New court filings identify Rep. Ilhan Omar by another name, Nur Said Elmi, and President Trump is calling on her to resign, claiming she used a false name to get elected. A 1997 marriage certificate published by the New York Post lists the same family name. We go through the filings, the certificate and what the Justice Department says about its probe.

Ilhan Omar calls the probe right-wing conspiracy theories laundered through the Justice Department, while a DOJ official rejects claims it is politically motivated. With Trump demanding her resignation, the question is whether the paper trail can actually threaten her seat. We lay out what is documented and what is still only alleged.

Ilhan Omar dodged questions on the immigration probe again, while court filings and a 1997 marriage certificate put her past back on the table. Trump says she must resign. We walk through the records and ask why she answers with attacks on the DOJ instead of documents.

intro.plain: New court filings identify Ilhan Omar by another name, and President Trump is now calling on her to resign. The New York Post has published a 1997 marriage certificate tied to the same family name, and a DOJ official says the probe is not political. Let me walk you through what is documented. Chat, should a member of Congress have to answer this publicly?
intro.mid: Ilhan Omar says this is a right-wing conspiracy pushed through the DOJ. The DOJ says it is not political. Meanwhile court filings use another name for her, and Trump wants her out of Congress. I want to separate what is on paper from what is just loud. Chat, do you think this ends with her losing her seat?
intro.bold: Ilhan Omar dodged questions on the immigration probe again, and the paper trail keeps growing: court filings with another name, a 1997 marriage certificate, and now the President telling her to resign. Her answer is to attack the DOJ. That is not an answer. Chat, what is the one question you would put to her today?

hook.plain: New court filings identify Ilhan Omar by another name, and President Trump says she must resign. Here is what the documents show and what is still only alleged.
hook.mid: A 1997 marriage certificate, a DOJ probe and a resignation demand from the President. Ilhan Omar calls it a conspiracy. Let's look at what is actually on paper.
hook.bold: Ilhan Omar keeps walking away from reporters, but the documents are not going anywhere. Court filings now use another name for her, and the President wants her gone.

descs.t: James Talarico leads Ken Paxton in a new poll of the Texas Senate race as early voting continues. By day 4, as of October 23, 2,883,923 Texans had voted, about 29.7% of projected final turnout. We walk through the poll, the early vote count and what it means for the race.

A new poll has Democrat James Talarico ahead of Ken Paxton in Texas, and Republicans are urging their voters to turn out before it is too late. Critics accuse Talarico of wanting open borders and an end to the Texas oil industry, while his supporters are marching to the polls. We break down where the Texas Senate race really stands.

Texas, a Republican stronghold, is suddenly in play: James Talarico leads Ken Paxton in a new poll with early voting underway. Republicans warn that staying home handed Arizona and Georgia to Democrats, and they say Texas is next. We look at what Talarico stands for on the border and energy, and whether Paxton can close the gap.

intro.plain: A new poll has James Talarico ahead of Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, and early voting is already well underway. By day 4 2,883,923 Texans had voted, about 29.7% of the projected turnout. That makes Texas a real contest this year. So tell me in the chat: is this poll real, or will Republicans still win Texas?
intro.mid: Texas Republicans are worried. A new poll puts Democrat James Talarico ahead of Ken Paxton, and with early voting underway Republicans are telling their voters to show up, pointing at Arizona and Georgia as warnings. Talarico's critics say he wants open borders and an end to Texas oil. Chat, tell me: does Paxton hold on, or does Texas flip?
intro.bold: Texas, a Republican stronghold, is in play. A new poll has James Talarico ahead of Ken Paxton while Texans are already voting. Republicans say Talarico would reopen the border and gut Texas oil, and they say staying home cost them Arizona and Georgia. Chat, one question: if Texas goes blue, what does that mean for America?

hook.plain: Day 4 of early voting in Texas, 2,883,923 votes cast, and a new poll has Talarico ahead of Paxton. Here is what the numbers actually show.
hook.mid: A Democrat leading in a Texas Senate poll, with voting already underway. Republicans are alarmed, and here is why this race is closer than anyone expected.
hook.bold: Texas could go blue. Talarico leads Paxton in a new poll, millions have already voted, and Republicans are warning their base: show up or lose the state.

Lisa's PRESS PLAY is charting around the world and reached number 2 on US iTunes, while some online voices have knocked the project. Tarantino debuted at number 44 on Global Spotify and topped YouTube's worldwide trending charts. We look at what the numbers say about her solo career.

Lisa is back and PRESS PLAY took the top spot on iTunes worldwide, with Tarantino ranking number 1 on YouTube's Worldwide Trending Videos chart. Her fans pushed every song onto the charts. Here is how the debut unfolded and what it means for her next move.

intro.plain: Lisa's new release PRESS PLAY debuted at number one on the Worldwide iTunes Album chart, and her single Tarantino opened at number 44 on Global Spotify with 1,911,491 streams. It is also number two on US iTunes. Chat, have you heard it yet, and is it her best solo work?

descs.t: The full Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 11 to 6 that ICE detainees with pending immigration cases have no constitutional right to a bond hearing, however long they are held. We explain what the en banc decision says and who it covers.

In an 11 to 6 en banc decision, the Fifth Circuit held that people who entered the US illegally and were arrested by ICE in the interior can be detained without bond for the whole of their removal proceedings. The majority and the dissent clashed hard, and Rep. Jayapal called it misguided. We walk through both sides of the ruling.

A major win for Trump's deportation push: the full Fifth Circuit ruled that ICE detainees have no constitutional right to a bond hearing, even after decades in the US, according to reports on the decision. We break down what it means for ICE, for detainees and for the fight still to come.

intro.plain: Big immigration ruling. The full Fifth Circuit voted 11 to 6 that ICE detainees with pending immigration cases have no constitutional right to a bond hearing, however long they are held. That means people can stay detained for their entire removal case. Chat, what do you think: right call, or does it go too far?
intro.mid: The Trump administration just won a major court fight. The full Fifth Circuit ruled 11 to 6 that people arrested by ICE can be held without bond for their whole deportation case. The judges clashed hard, and Democrats like Pramila Jayapal are calling it misguided. Chat, tell me: does this end up at the Supreme Court?
intro.bold: This is a huge win for deportations. The full Fifth Circuit says people who came here illegally and were arrested by ICE have no constitutional right to a bond hearing, even if they have lived here for decades. Eleven judges to six. Chat, one question: should every illegal entrant be held until their case is decided?

hook.plain: Eleven judges to six: ICE detainees with pending immigration cases have no constitutional right to a bond hearing. Here is what the ruling says.
hook.mid: Held for the whole deportation case, with no bond hearing. The Fifth Circuit just handed ICE a major win, and here is why the judges split.
hook.bold: No bond, no matter how long. The full Fifth Circuit just sided with ICE, and the dissenting judges are furious. Here is why.

descs.t: The US Justice Department has sued to block certification of Alaska's Senate election result if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, Reuters and NBC News report. Trump says he ordered the suit. We explain what the lawsuit asks for and what happens next.

Trump's Justice Department filed a lawsuit that could block certification of Alaska's Senate race if Dan Sullivan loses. Peltola called it a desperate attempt to silence Alaskans, while some on the right say critics are misreading what the suit actually targets, pointing to two Sullivans on the ballot. We go through both cases.

Alaska's Senate seat is now a legal fight before the result is even in. Democrats from Gavin Newsom to Ro Khanna say Trump's DOJ is trying to steal an election, and Trump says he ordered the suit himself. We look at what the lawsuit says, what each side claims and what comes next.

intro.plain: The Justice Department has sued over Alaska's Senate race, asking to block certification if Republican Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola. Trump says he ordered it. Democrats are calling it an attempt to steal the election, and some Republicans say the suit is being misread. Chat, have you read what it actually says?
intro.mid: Alaska's Senate race is in court before the votes are even counted. Trump's DOJ wants to be able to block certification if Dan Sullivan loses, Peltola calls it a desperate attempt to silence Alaskans, and some say the real issue is two Sullivans on the ballot. Chat, tell me: legitimate case or political move?
intro.bold: Trump's Justice Department just went to court to stop Alaska's Senate result from being certified if Dan Sullivan loses. Democrats are screaming that an election is being stolen. Others say the lawsuit is about a confusing ballot with two Sullivans on it. Chat, one question: who is telling the truth about this lawsuit?

hook.plain: The Justice Department is suing to block Alaska's Senate result if Dan Sullivan loses. Here is what the lawsuit asks for.
hook.mid: A Senate race in court before the votes are counted, and two Sullivans on one ballot. Here is what is really going on in Alaska.
hook.bold: Democrats say Trump is trying to steal Alaska's Senate seat. Trump says he ordered the suit. Here is what the lawsuit really says.
